title: Pod signer uses a one-shot loadFailed latch: a transient key-load failure permanently disables signing for the process lifetime

If the signer fails to load once (file absent during first boot, a race with another process writing the key file, a transient I/O error), the latch engages and never retries. With `requireSigned` on, every subsequent pod request throws `SigningUnavailable`. With it off, every request goes unsigned.
failure: During a container restart, the sovereign identity file is being written by bootstrap while management-api starts and attempts its first pod write. The load fails transiently, the latch engages, and for the entire remaining uptime of the management-api process (potentially weeks), no pod write can be signed. Nobody notices until a pod write fails WAC verification or goes out unsigned.
confidence: high

confidence: high on the missing sync; the incident requires a power/OS-level crash

title: Candidate formatting writes to files outside the evaluated worktree
evidence: substring check candidate.rs:115; rustfmt on control plane candidate.rs:129-131; canary write reproduced in the 1 November audit; ADR-DE-009's documented confinement is contradicted by the probe (DE-02.2 Tension); repair present only at bf3a11d (DE-06.1); pins at services/dream-engine/Cargo.toml:26-27; DE-01 states the current running version was not requalified.

title: The published change is not the change that was evaluated

confidence: high that the identity gap exists at the pinned versions; inferred that a production night exercised it — no live-host claim exists in the material.

title: Retained evidence is overwritten, so the night cannot be reconstructed

confidence: high for the mechanisms (all reproduced); inferred that the incident relied on them.

title: Replay, payment and trail state are process-local; restart and replicas reopen the windows, and a zero TTL disables replay checks entirely
evidence: "Restart forgets ids, replicas do not share state. Reuse is possible while the token remains fresh" (replay_store.rs:115); TTL "is not validated against token freshness. Environment accepts any positive seconds. Constructor also permits zero" (replay.rs:133, :149) — with TTL 0 the seen-entry check `age < TTL` fails and the store takes the "overwrite same slot, accept" branch (replay.rs:260), i.e. every replay is admitted (this last step is inferred from the stated flow). Trail and epoch locks are "in-process and held across network calls — a known gap that a second replica does not share" (CHANGELOG.md:603; trail_store.rs:340); the freshness window alone is ±60 s (nip98.rs:28).

confidence: high (source defect, open at `c27cdfed` per the successor's own scope); reachability is inferred — it requires an operator running payments against value on a network the attacker will fund

confidence: medium (the shipped-pin defect is stated with high confidence; the triggering configuration and the value of exposed content are deployment facts the material cannot show — inferred)
